source.title: L0 is not a neutral hyperparameter

page_placements.theme: Hierarchical absorption, hedging and sparse-coding optima

record.tranche_reason: It varies SAE L0 in a toy model and measures whether the learned dictionary recovers the known features, a conceptual test of SAE-feature recovery rather than a reproduction of the original toy-network superposition method.
record.gate_note: The post reports its own toy-model SAE experiments on feature recovery under different L0 settings. It does not test whether a network with more features than dimensions represents them as overlapping directions: the toy model has 20 true features and the SAE has 20 latents. Cited results from other work and comment-thread claims are not recorded as experimental rows.
record.test_reason: In a toy setting with known ground-truth features, the post varies SAE L0 and shows learned latents match the true features only at the right L0 (or with a mixed-L0 loss). It argues SAE features depend on a hyperparameter, so the post bears on whether dictionary features are canonical units (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors also argue that L0 should not be treated as an arbitrary hyperparameter: a 'correct' L0 should be assumed and sought. They suggest a multi-L0 loss may help when the true L0 is unknown.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a Global BatchTopK SAE trained on correlated toy features and varies its L0; it does not reproduce the original Toy Models of Superposition method or test a network with more features than dimensions.
record.method_sensitivity: The recovered features differ with SAE L0; frequency affects which latents are most broken. The combined-loss result differs between lambda=1 and lambda=20.

fits_no_version.finding: At k=4, a broken hedging SAE gets lower MSE (0.42) than the correct SAE cut to k=4 (0.53).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: When SAE L0 is below the true L0, the reconstruction objective rewards learning mixed (hedged) latents over the true features.

record.problems: Evidence is from one toy setup with 20 true features and 20 SAE latents, not a real network or LLM. Feature-recovery outcomes are mostly qualitative descriptions of plots, with no reported uncertainty, numerical recovery scores, or stated control runs.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported experimental results bearing on the listed versions were left out. Cited findings and discussion-thread comments were excluded.

untested.parts: The toy features are mutually orthogonal and the SAE width equals the feature count. There is no superposition, no sparsity-dependent transition and no geometry measured.
Network neuron capacity and polysemanticity are not studied.
No test of polysemantic neurons arising without capacity pressure.
Stability across seeds or runs, real-model SAEs, width effects (mentioned only in comments, citing other work), and completeness with more features than latents are not tested.
No comparison of 1-D with multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: This is a single toy setup with qualitative, plot-based outcomes and no uncertainty. The toy features are orthogonal and the SAE width equals the feature count, so the post speaks to whether SAEs recover ground truth, not to superposition itself. The tranche was changed from T2 to T5 because the post's thrust is that SAE features depend on a hyperparameter.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test a network with more sparse features than dimensions, or measure superposition geometry or a sparsity-dependent transition in such a network.
The study constrains an SAE's L0, not the capacity of network neurons or dimensions; it does not test whether neurons become polysemantic because of competition for representational capacity.
It does not test polysemantic neurons arising independently of capacity pressure.
It studies a toy model, not LLM activations or SAE feature recovery from an LLM.

It tests recovery of known toy-model features under specified SAE L0 settings, but not feature stability across runs or models, nor whether SAE features are canonical units of a real model's representation.
It does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.
